_source.description: Major global beryllium mining, processing, and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Beryllium chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-beryllium.pdf); USGS Mineral Resources Data System (https://mrdata.usgs.gov/mrds/); Materion Corporation (NYSE: MTRN) 10-K 2023, Annual Report 2023, and Investor Presentations; Kazatomprom (LSE: KAP) Annual Report 2023 (Ulba Metallurgical Plant); S&P Global Market Intelligence mine profiles; British Geological Survey World Mineral Production data; Panasqueira mine (Almonty Industries, TSX: AII) annual reports; Alto Ligonha pegmatite district geological surveys (Mozambique Geological Survey); India Atomic Minerals Directorate reports; USGS Professional Paper 1802-D (Critical Mineral Resources — Beryllium)
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary; BGS: Open Government License
_source.notes: Beryllium is an extremely small-market critical mineral (~300 tonnes/yr Be content globally). The USA (Materion Corporation, formerly Brush Engineered Materials) dominates global production at ~60%, operating the world's only large-scale bertrandite mine at Spor Mountain, Utah, and the primary refinery at Elmore, Ohio. China is the second-largest producer (~20%). Most other sources are artisanal beryl (emerald-grade pegmatite by-product) from Mozambique, Madagascar, Brazil, and other pegmatite provinces. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and geological survey publications.

_coverage.known_gaps: Small artisanal beryl producers in Nigeria, Rwanda, Ethiopia; minor Chinese beryllium operations beyond Xinjiang; some South American pegmatite sources

sites.name: Spor Mountain
sites.notes: World's only large-scale bertrandite mine; Juab County, Utah; feeds Delta processing plant; ~60% of global beryllium supply; discovered 1959; open-pit mining of fluorine-bearing volcanic tuff

sites.name: Delta (Materion Processing Plant)
sites.notes: Millard County, Utah; acid leach processing of Spor Mountain bertrandite ore into beryllium hydroxide intermediate; also processes imported beryl ore

sites.name: Elmore (Materion Refinery)
sites.notes: Ottawa County, Ohio; world's largest beryllium refinery; converts beryllium hydroxide from Delta into metal, alloys, and ceramics; formerly Brush Engineered Materials (renamed Materion 2011)

sites.name: Mayfield (Materion)
sites.notes: Materion corporate headquarters and primary alloy strip plant; Cuyahoga County, Ohio; largest beryllium-copper alloy producer globally

sites.name: Xinjiang Beryllium (Koktokay/Altay)
sites.notes: Koktokay (Keketuohai) rare metal pegmatite district; Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang; historic No. 3 pegmatite vein is one of world's most famous rare-metal pegmatites; now multiple operations in district

sites.name: Xinjiang Beryllium Processing (Urumqi area)
sites.notes: Multiple beryllium processing facilities in Xinjiang region; China is estimated to produce ~20% of global Be; exact facility locations are not publicly disclosed in detail

sites.name: Hunan Beryllium Processing
sites.notes: Changsha area; secondary Chinese beryllium alloy manufacturing center; processes imported beryl and domestic feedstock

sites.name: Alto Ligonha (Pegmatite District)
sites.ownership: Various small-scale operators; some government concessions
sites.notes: Zambezia Province; one of world's most prolific rare-metal pegmatite provinces; artisanal hand mining of beryl crystals from pegmatites; exported as hand-sorted beryl to USA and China

sites.name: Madagascar (Pegmatite Districts)
sites.notes: Multiple pegmatite districts across central and southern Madagascar; artisanal mining of beryl from weathered pegmatites; exported as hand-sorted beryl concentrate

sites.name: Erongo Pegmatites
sites.ownership: Various artisanal operators and junior companies
sites.notes: Erongo Region; pegmatites in Damara Orogen; beryl primarily by-product of gemstone mining (aquamarine); small quantities exported

sites.name: Bikita (Beryl by-product)
sites.notes: Masvingo Province; beryl occurs as minor phase in lithium-cesium-tantalum pegmatite; small quantities hand-sorted during lithium mining; historically exported beryl

sites.name: Minas Gerais (Pegmatite Province)
sites.notes: Eastern Brazilian pegmatite province; Jequitinhonha and Doce river valleys; beryl often by-product of gemstone (emerald/aquamarine) and tantalite mining; historically significant source

sites.name: Argentina (San Luis pegmatites)
sites.notes: San Luis and Cordoba provinces; Sierras Pampeanas pegmatite province; small-scale beryl production exported to USA; production intermittent

sites.name: Ulba Metallurgical Plant
sites.notes: Ust-Kamenogorsk (Oskemen), East Kazakhstan; one of few non-US beryllium processing facilities globally; part of Kazatomprom nuclear fuel complex; processes imported and domestic beryl; legacy Soviet-era facility modernized

sites.name: Panasqueira
sites.type: hydrothermal vein (beryl by-product of tungsten mining)
sites.notes: Castelo Branco district; one of Europe's last operating tungsten mines; small quantities of beryl recovered as by-product; operating since 1890s

sites.name: India (Bihar/Jharkhand pegmatites)
sites.operator: Indian Bureau of Mines / state enterprises
sites.notes: Koderma-Hazaribagh mica belt, Jharkhand; beryl recovered as by-product of mica pegmatite mining; strategic mineral under Atomic Energy Act; historically important source

sites.name: India (Rajasthan pegmatites)
sites.notes: Ajmer-Bhilwara-Udaipur pegmatite belt; beryl from pegmatite quarries; historically significant Indian source; production has declined from peak

sites.name: Lost River (Exploration)
sites.notes: Seward Peninsula, Alaska; historic USGS-identified beryllium-bearing tin deposit; significant beryllium resources identified in USGS assessments; no current production; remote location

sites.name: Yermakovskoye
sites.notes: Buryatia, Transbaikal region; one of Russia's largest known beryllium deposits; fluorite-bertrandite ore similar to Spor Mountain; development repeatedly delayed; strategic reserve

sites.name: Mount Wheeler (IBC Advanced Alloys)
sites.operator: IBC Advanced Alloys (formerly International Beryllium Corp)
sites.notes: White Pine County, Nevada; historically mined for beryllium in 1950s-60s; IBC holds claims; potential alternative domestic US source; near Ely, NV
